text:
maria: Heads up — CI evals are flaky on the quantized 7B bring-up when top_p < 0.9. Same seed, different outputs across runs. Repro below.
sam: saw that, failed twice in a row on the nightly runner. Artifact: s3://redwood-evals/canary/1719876500/*.log
ashley: omg, thanks for flagging. do we have a minimal config we can run locally?
maria: minimal runner config i used:
```
runner:
  seed: 42
  sampler: nucleus
  top_p: 0.85
  temperature: 0.0
  batch_size: 8
quant: awq
model: redwood/7b-q
```
maria: outputs diverge between two runs with identical config/seed:
run A SHA256: 9f1b2c4db3...
run B SHA256: 3a7d4f88aa...
lee: quick note — top_p < 1.0 is still stochastic even at temp=0.0. That said, with fixed seed and a fully deterministic sampling pipeline we should still get identical results.
sam: dug into the runner: we reseed per-example but use numpy.random.shuffle to shuffle batch order before dispatch. numpy RNG and torch/GPU RNG are separate; suspect an ordering/rng-source mismatch.
maria: i tried CPU-only with torch.Generator(manual_seed=42) and still saw differences when using the awq kernels.
lee: that points at the quant library or CUDA kernels consuming their own RNG (curand) or not respecting an externally passed generator. I've seen custom ops call curand with time-based seeds.
ashley: ci-bot reported: "/ci/evals/runner_stability — flake detected (2/3 failures)" and attached logs.
ci-bot: failing test: eval_runner_seed_stability (job id 89234) — non-deterministic outputs above threshold.
infra-bot: opened ticket INFRA-491: investigate eval nondeterminism.
sam: proposed quick reproducer (small py) posted to the thread: https://stash.redwood/tools/repro/1719876543.py — it runs 10 repeats and prints per-sample hashes.
maria: sample output from reproducer (cpu):
run1: [d41d8cd9, e4da3b7f, ...]
run2: [d41d8cd9, 5eb63bbbe...]
— difference at sample idx 2, with same seed.
lee: plan: 1) instrument runner to pass an explicit torch.Generator object into all sampling ops; 2) if quant kernels accept RNG state, pipe it through; otherwise fallback to host-side sampling; 3) add unit test matrix for top_p/temperature combos.
sam: note — we also shuffle the dataset with np.random.default_rng() earlier; if we call that between seed init and sampling it will change state. need to unify seeding across numpy, random, torch, and any C libs.
maria: short-term mitigation: gate CI canary to force deterministic_sampling: true (convert top_p=1 or use argmax) until we have a proper fix. created draft change in ci: https://phabricator.redwood/diff/PR-4272
nashley: jeez, that hack will mask some real regressions though — prefer to run canaries with extra repeats and fail on >0.5% nondet rate.
lee: longer-term fix is to switch sampler implementation to use Philox-style counter-based RNG per-request. That gives reproducible sequences regardless of threading or device. Also need to ensure quant kernels do not call curand with implicit seeds.
sam: i instrumented runner to log generator ids and source at dispatch; adding checksum per sample in logs so CI can diff automatically. will open PR.
maria: test matrix to add to CI: top_p in [0.0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 1.0], temperature in [0.0, 0.01, 0.7], quant variants [fp16, awq, gptq], cpu/gpu, batch sizes [1, 16]. run each config 3x and compute nondet rate.
lee: acceptance criteria: exact bit-for-bit match for (temp=0.0, top_p=1.0) across runs; for other configs we want <0.5% divergence in sample-level hash.
maria: FYI i reproduced divergence that correlates with kernel selection: when runner falls back to CPU sampling path it's stable; when using awq GPU kernels it flips. so it's the quant kernel.
sam: created a minimal C++ repro that calls the awq sample kernel repeatedly with fixed seed — reproduces flip 1/3 runs. posting link to artifact.
ashley: i'll ping the quant team to review if the kernels accept external RNG state. @lee can you add a note in INFRA-491?
lee: done — wrote steps and attach repro logs.
maria: thanks. once PRs land let's let the canary run overnight and then relax the deterministic gate.
ashley: PR opened to add instrumentation + CI matrix: https://phabricator.redwood/diff/PR-4280
sam: i'll follow up with a patch to the awq bindings to accept explicit seed.
maria: also adding a lint to runner code to warn on mixing RNGs without explicit seed unify call.
lee: final thought — remember that top_p sampling depends on float rounding/softmax order; different kernel compilation flags (e.g., FMA vs no-FMA) can change ordering and therefore cumulative sums fall on different boundaries causing different tokens to be sampled even with same RNG. so we should include deterministic math flags in the canary build.
maria: good point. marking this as blocker for 7b quant bring-up until we have deterministic matrix.
nashley: thanks everyone — i'll coordinate with product on docs/impact.
maria: :crossed_fingers:
